articles.title: I camped in one of Britain’s last remaining rainforests
articles.summary: A fragment of temperate rainforest lies on the edge of Dartmoor, and following years of conservation work, its owners have now opened up a sustainable campsite next to this fragile ecosystem.
body: Mist blankets the valley as I wheel my camping gear down the small hill towards a clearing ringed by trees and shrubs. A picnic bench sits at its edge, angled towards the reason why I’m here: one of the last remaining fragments of temperate rainforest in Britain. I’m pitching my tent at Wray Valley Camping, a low-impact site on Dartmoor’s eastern edge between Lustleigh and Moretonhampstead, where I’ll spend five days on one of the site’s “nearly wild” pitches.

Also known as Atlantic woodland, temperate rainforests depend on a rare combination of high humidity, rainfall and consistently mild coastal temperatures where the sea moderates the climate. They once stretched from the western Highlands of Scotland down to Cornwall, covering 20% of the UK, and sheltering rare and delicate lichens and plants. Today more than 95% of our temperate rainforest cover is gone, but Devon’s near-constant dampness and its exposure to the Atlantic make it one of the last strongholds for this rare habitat.
Wray Valley Camping owners Michelle Grist and her partner Kevin Chamberlain have spent seven years restoring this fragile ecosystem while developing the adjacent campsite.
points: A fragment of temperate rainforest lies on the edge of Dartmoor, and following years of conservation work, its owners have now opened up a sustainable campsite next to this fragile ecosystem.

articles.title: Rachel Roddy’s summer minestrone with pesto – recipe | A kitchen in Rome
articles.summary: A fresh, seasonal vegetable soup that can be made in advance and only improves in texture and flavour over time. Now that I am an accomplished sourdough maker, soon to start my own micro-bakery and YouTube channel … Only joking!
body: It is a shame, then, that I didn’t give the same attention to the pan of summer minestrone I had felt so pleased with myself for cooking, cutting the courgettes carefully so they looked like Trivial Pursuit scoring wedges, while drinking tea and listening for the bottle bank lorry to drop the glass into its box, and before the sun (or anyone else) was up. Even though the combined taste of minestrone and milky Yorkshire tea is interesting, I knew it had turned out particularly well. I put on the lid, left the pan at the back of the stove and went out.

It must have been 11am by the time I got back home with a plant of basil quietly suffocating behind its plastic cone. The kitchen was already hot and the minestrone was only slightly, but unequivocally, fizzy. A spoonful of pesto did not balance it out – but please don’t let my neglect put you off making this abundantly fresh-green and creamy-white courgette, green and white bean minestrone, inspired by three recipes in Laura Ragoni’s Profumi e Sapori di Liguria.
points: A fresh, seasonal vegetable soup that can be made in advance and only improves in texture and flavour over time.

articles.title: The Story Behind Kelly Wearstler’s “Timeless” H&M Home Collaboration
articles.summary: “It’s affordable, but the quality is still there,” Kelly Wearstler tells Vogue of the collection, which spans homewares and fashion—and is available to shop.
body: On a busy street near the Duomo in Milan this past April, the usual scenes you’d expect to unfold on a frenetic morning in the city were visible: the yellow trams rumbling by, locals sipping their espressos from zinc counters, well-dressed members of the city’s design and fashion sets whizzing past on bicycles.

And if you’d followed one of the latter, you’d very likely have ended up at Palazzo Acerbi, a 17th-century Baroque palace on the Corso di Porto Romano. Or, more specifically, in its central courtyard, admiring a soaring installation of a gridded wooden sculpture. More curiously, when you looked closer, you would have noticed that they were actually modular chairs, stacked in a cascading wave like a kind of contemporary ziggurat.

Throughout the rooms, Kelly Wearstler herself was buzzing around in a gray tailored jumpsuit, enthusiastically explaining the details behind every piece—and the cleverly conceived installations that showcased it, created in collaboration with the fashion-favorite design practice Studio Boum.

articles.title: You be the judge: should my girlfriend stop letting the recycling pile up?
articles.summary: Robin keeps used packaging on the kitchen ledge. Benny thinks that’s unhygienic. You decide who’s talking rubbish. • Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror. We’ve had little flies buzzing around – I know they’re coming from the recycling.
body: My girlfriend, Robin, likes to keep the recycling on a ledge above the counter in our kitchen, instead of taking it straight outside. I absolutely hate it. It’s not just empty cereal boxes or clean bottles – we have a dog, so there are often empty dog food cans too. There’s always a bit of food left around the edges, and if they’re left for long enough they start to smell and attract flies. It’s gross.

We live in a flat on the third floor, so I understand not wanting to make a trip to the bin every time we finish something, but there has to be a limit. If the cans are growing mould or attracting flies, we’ve passed it. I don’t want to be preparing food while there’s a collection of old things sitting above the counter.

I’ve suggested rinsing the cans as soon as we’ve used them, which Robin does sometimes, but not often. We have a small kitchen and clear surfaces make it feel calmer and cleaner. Twelve pieces of recycling lined up along the wall is an eyesore.
points: Robin keeps used packaging on the kitchen ledge.

articles.title: I used to think I was an ambivalent mother, then my child started to stutter | Bridie Jabour
articles.summary: I snapped at my children. Resented daily pickup. But I was there when he needed me, and my perception of myself completely changed. I still can’t pinpoint when it happened, but it felt as though my child lost the ability to communicate overnight.
body: Of course, that is not what happened, and he never lost the ability to communicate. But it felt as though he did at the time. And even with the benefit of hindsight, it felt like he went from a chatty three-year-old to being unable to get a sentence out. “W-w-w-w-w-w-w-w-w-what c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-can I-I-I-I-I-I-I” and then silence as he gave up trying and just looked up at me.

I often joke my parenting approach is one of benign neglect, and that I lack any instinct at all. I still do lean into that caricature at times (“I will have to do a few minutes of parenting this weekend,” I recently texted the family group chat in mock horror). This joke originated when I first became a mother more than eight years ago. I perpetuated this idea that my children were not the centre of my world and therefore I was somehow different from other mothers.
Privately I thought I was more ambivalent about motherhood than I anticipated. It turns out I had mistaken what maternal ambivalence was.
points: But I was there when he needed me, and my perception of myself completely changed.

articles.title: Elie Saab Makes It Real With an H&M Collaboration That Brings His Red-Carpet Style Within Reach
articles.summary: Come October 22, the Elie Saab H&M collaboration at last puts Mr. Saab’s particular brand of glamour—spotted of late on Zendaya, Olivia Dean, and Eva Longoria—within reach for the rest of us.
body: Despite 40-plus years of dazzling red-carpet moments—and two decades since becoming the first Arab designer on the official Paris haute couture calendar —in real life Elie Saab is still more comfortable letting his runway do the talking for him. And while he’s often been approached about collaborations, it took until now to feel the time was right.

“We’ve always been true to ourselves,” the soft-spoken couturier with 20 million followers said during an exclusive preview at his showroom in Paris. “We’ve never been driven by trends. If you look across the archives, what you see is consistency and craftsmanship.” He continued: “We wanted to be sure we could do something where every piece was special—without compromise—because otherwise it wouldn’t be Elie Saab. No one wants ‘basic’ from Elie Saab.”
There’s nothing basic about this evening look from the Elie Saab H&M collaboration.
This bustier top and pants are among the 55 pieces in the collection.
points: Come October 22, the Elie Saab H&M collaboration at last puts Mr. Saab’s particular brand of glamour—spotted of late on Zendaya, Olivia Dean, and Eva Longoria—within reach for the rest of us.

articles.title: How CEO Olivier Bron Capitalized on Bloomingdale’s Big Moment
articles.summary: Saks Global’s bankruptcy became an opportunity for Bloomingdale’s, which had been laying the groundwork to win in a difficult market for the last three years under Bron.
body: Olivier Bron likes a challenge. That’s what led him to his job as CEO of Bloomingdale’s in 2023, after spending years leading retailers abroad, first at Galeries Lafayette in Paris, then at Central Group in Bangkok. He was drawn to the US market, but couldn’t understand why it lagged so far behind international players when it came to its department stores — once the crown jewels of American retail.

“When I came here, I was very surprised. I visited hundreds of department stores, and none of the best department stores in the world were actually located in the US,” says Bron, speaking from his office at Bloomingdale’s HQ in Long Island City, New York. “So I saw that as a fantastic opportunity for Bloomingdale’s.”

articles.title: The New Rules for Raising Money in Fashion
articles.summary: After years of chasing hype and scale, investors are looking for something harder to manufacture: sustainable growth, profitability and a brand customers genuinely want.
body: When fashion was in the grips of its growth-at-all-costs era, investors were backing buzz and brands were blowing up — but bottom lines weren’t. Now, in the midst of a subdued market, investors are being more selective, and the new playbook for funding fashion has a lot to do with the quality of that growth, the depth of connection with customers and the founder’s individual appeal.

“Investors have not lost their appetite for fashion; they have become much more discerning about the businesses they are prepared to back,” says Lorna Hopkinson, M&A managing director in the retail and consumer team at business advisory firm BDO. “There is still an appetite for good transactions, but the gap between strong and weaker businesses has become more pronounced.”

That’s largely owed to a reality that there’s too much competition in fashion, too much inventory and too many markdowns, says John Kernan, a seasoned retail market analyst and former managing director at TD Cowen, speaking in an independent capacity.
points: After years of chasing hype and scale, investors are looking for something harder to manufacture: sustainable growth, profitability and a brand customers genuinely want.

articles.title: It’s Time to Take Ranch Dressing Seriously
articles.summary: You can tell a lot about someone by the way they talk about ranch dressing. Do they express Midwestern passion for the condiment, or coastal-elite distaste? Do they limit its usage to crisp iceberg lettuce salads, or do they become a jester of pairings, drizzling the sauce over steak, pasta, and…
body: Ranch dressing was first invented in 1954 by a contractor named Steve Henson, with the original recipe consisting of buttermilk, mayonnaise, and various herbs and seasonings. Initially, Henson served the dressing to his workers to help liven up their salads; as its popularity soared, he began serving it out of a rustic, 1800s-stagecoach-turned-restaurant called Cold Spring Tavern in the Santa Ynez mountains of California, where it’s still served to this day. Early DIY packets of the sauce, which were whipped up at Henson’s Hidden Valley Ranch (yes, a real place ), were marketed as a party dip — a foreshadowing detail of its crowd-pleasing talents.

articles.title: The Distinctly Brazilian Flavor of São Paolo's Japanese Cuisine
articles.summary: From Nipo-Brazilian cuisine that relies on Amazonian fish to home-cooking-inspired izakayas to traditional omakase, São Paulo’s Japanese restaurants are richer and more varied than ever before.
body: At Aizomê, a stylish Japanese restaurant shrouded by a thick wall of trees just off São Paulo ’s main thoroughfare, Avenida Paulista, the food is both recognizable to devotees of Japanese cuisine and distinctly Brazilian. You might find pirarucu, an enormous Amazonian riverfish, in saikyo yaki, a traditional Japanese sweet-miso preparation more commonly used on black cod. Ponzu incorporates tucupi, a tart yellow sauce made from fermented wild manioc, a root native to the Amazon.

“I’m third generation,” says owner Telma Shiraishi, who was born and raised in São Paulo and whose grandparents hail from the Wakayama and Iwate prefectures of Japan. “It doesn’t make sense for me to make a cuisine that is 100% Japanese, bringing 100% of ingredients from Japan.”
Telma Shiraishi has led Aizomê for two decades, bringing Brazilian ingredients and Japanese techniques under one roof.
points: From Nipo-Brazilian cuisine that relies on Amazonian fish to home-cooking-inspired izakayas to traditional omakase, São Paulo’s Japanese restaurants are richer and more varied than ever before.
